name: La Shawn Ford
call_status: confirmed winner (safe D seat; Wikipedia lists him as member-elect, term from 3 Jan 2027)

bio.education: BA elementary education (minor political science), Loyola University Chicago; attended Niles College Seminary and UIC
bio.career: Former Chicago Public Schools history teacher/basketball coach; real-estate broker (Ford Desired Real Estate, 2001)
bio.prior_office: Illinois House of Representatives, 8th district, 2007–2027 (former chair, Appropriations–Higher Education); 2019 Chicago mayoral candidate

self_description: Told WTTW after the primary that the party should 'unite' and 'be as progressive [as] possible' (auto-transcript); otherwise runs as a constituent-services/health-care Democrat endorsed by retiring Rep. Danny Davis.
primary_context: Won a 13-candidate open primary (17 Mar 2026) with ~24–29% over Chicago Treasurer Melissa Conyears-Ervin (backed by ~$500k+ from AIPAC's United Democracy Project) and progressive Kina Collins; Fairshake (crypto) spent ~$2.5M attacking Ford over his state crypto-regulation vote. Contest was over experience/machine backing more than ideology.

L3.e: In post-primary WTTW interview said Democrats must restore Obamacare and 'that is Medicare for all' (auto-generated transcript; did not answer the M4A question at a March forum)

C5.e: Confirmed Fraternal Order of Police endorsement when challenged by Kina Collins at a West Side forum: 'The endorsement means that I will hold them accountable.'

EPD.note: 19 years in the Illinois House (authored legislative record, chaired Approps–Higher Ed, created Black-community economic commission); BA only; campaign platform fairly general (ACA restoration, seniors' Medicare task force, Medicaid-for-housing, supervised drug-use sites, regulated hemp).

EO.note: Attended multiple primary candidate forums (Collins Academy 27 Jan; West Side forum March) but a 'Debate Illinois 7' petition demanded a formal debate; no general-election debate with Republican Chad Koppie found. Media mostly local/public outlets (WTTW, N'DIGO, Austin Weekly). At the March forum he did not answer the Medicare-for-All question, using the time to rebut Collins (TRiiBE); responded to crypto attack ads with a cease-and-desist rather than substantive rebuttal.

outside_support: Opposed: Fairshake crypto super PAC (~$2.5M against)
Opposed indirectly: UDP/AIPAC backed rival Conyears-Ervin
notable_positions: Restore ACA subsidies and reverse 'Big Beautiful Bill' Medicaid cuts; prioritise safety-net hospitals/FQHCs (https://www.austinweeklynews.com/2026/02/02/7th-congressional-primary-candidates/)
Medicare for All named as the party's priority in WTTW interview (https://www.pbs.org/video/democratic-candidates-donna-miller-la-shawn-ford-on-their-congressional-races-w89km9)

Shift federal spending from defense and incarceration toward housing; use Medicaid to keep people housed (https://thetriibe.com/2026/03/il-07-candidates-describe-plans-to-address-affordable-housing-child-care-and-health-care-during-west-side-forum/)

Supports ending cash bail: 'No one should be sitting in jail because they can't afford $100' (https://thetriibe.com/2026/03/il-07-candidates-describe-plans-to-address-affordable-housing-child-care-and-health-care-during-west-side-forum/)
Has pushed regulated hemp sales and supervised drug-use sites on the West Side (https://www.axios.com/local/chicago/2026/02/12/illinois-7th-district-voter-guide)
rationale: Few left or centrist markers (M4A remark vs. FOP endorsement), so neither index is decisive. A long-serving state legislator (EPD 5) whose campaign was locally focused and generic, with no formal debates found and a documented dodge of the M4A question at a forum, so the rubric points to Cat 3; the evidence on engagement is thin and the call is borderline with a mainstream-party Cat 2/imperfect-fit reading.

bio.career: Sales/business owner; after Congress CEO of the Executives Club of Chicago, Midwest chair at JPMorgan Chase, CEO of Mesirow Wealth Advisors (2019)
bio.prior_office: U.S. House, IL-08, 2005–2011 (Blue Dog Coalition and New Democrat Coalition member; lost 2010)

primary_context: Won 8-way open primary (17 Mar 2026) with ~32% over Justice Democrats/Sanders/Warren/AOC-backed Junaid Ahmed (~26.5%) and Kevin Morrison; framed by Roll Call and The Prospect as moderate vs. progressive, with ~$4M from AIPAC-linked 'Elect Chicago Women' plus AI and crypto super PACs supporting her.

C3.e: Congressional record: one of 9 Democrats backing extension of capital-gains/dividend cuts (2005), one of 15 backing ~$70B Bush tax-cut extension (2006), voted to repeal the estate tax; no 2026 wealth-tax/rate-hike support found (historical evidence)

C7.e: Documented cross-party voting record 2005–11 (Bush tax-cut extensions, estate-tax repeal, CAFTA); described as 'perhaps the most conservative Democrat in Washington'

C8.e: Pro-trade record (one of 15 Democrats for CAFTA, costing AFL-CIO endorsement); backed in 2026 by pro-AI Leading the Future/Think Big ($1.1M) and crypto Protect Progress ($557k); former Executives Club of Chicago CEO

C1_endorsements: New Democrat Majority super PAC (~$935k IE in 2026 primary)

EPD.note: Former three-term member of Congress (Financial Services, Small Business; New Dem financial-services task force co-chair); senior executive career (CEO roles, JPMorgan); authored legislative record (Dodd-Frank preemption amendment).

EO.note: Took part in the Daily Herald primary forum (Jan 2026, ~300 attendees) with other Democrats; no general-election debate with Republican Jennifer Davis found. Campaign leaned heavily on paid TV (self and super PAC). Rival Ahmed accused her of attending an anti-ICE rally only for photos; rival Morrison called her 'MIA for nearly two decades'. No evidence found either way of substantive engagement with critics.

outside_support: Reps. Steny Hoyer, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Bill Foster, Brad Schneider, Scott Peters
notable_positions: Runs on her ACA vote ('architect of Obamacare'), saying it cost her re-election; defend health care from GOP cuts (https://rollcall.com/2026/03/18/illinois-house-election-democrats-melissa-bean/)

2026 mailers promise to 'kick ICE out of our communities'; questionnaire calls for pulling ICE from communities until reforms (bodycams, no masks, end agent immunity) (https://prospect.org/2026/03/12/illinois-eighth-congressional-district-aipac-ai-bean-ahmed/)

Comprehensive immigration reform while opposing mass deportation; previously opposed amnesty and backed employer penalties (https://www.nbcchicago.com/illinois-election-2026/melissa-bean-projected-to-win-8th-district-race-in-illinois-democratic-primary/3909567/?amp=1)
Congressional record: Bush tax-cut extensions, estate-tax repeal, CAFTA, stimulus, cap-and-trade, ACA (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melissa_Bean)
Pro-Israel record in office; backed by DMFI and AIPAC-linked super PAC (https://jewishinsider.com/2026/02/illinois-ad-buy-moderates-laura-fine-melissa-bean-donna-miller/)
rationale: No left-index markers found; centrist coalition ties (former Blue Dog/New Dem, New Democrat Majority spending) plus a documented cross-party fiscal and trade record and business/AI/crypto backing give CI around 6. Much of the centrist evidence is from her 2005–11 record rather than 2026 statements, and her 2026 immigration messaging ('kick ICE out') moved left, so confidence is Medium.

name: Daniel Biss

bio.career: University of Chicago math professor (2002–08); policy adviser to Gov. Pat Quinn; executive director, Rust Belt Rising
bio.prior_office: Illinois House 2011–13; Illinois Senate 2013–19; 2018 gubernatorial primary candidate; Mayor of Evanston 2021–Oct 2026

primary_context: Won 15-way open primary (17 Mar 2026) with ~29.5% over Kat Abughazaleh (~26%, left insurgent who called Gaza a genocide) and state Sen. Laura Fine (~20%, backed by AIPAC-aligned spending that also attacked Biss). Biss ran as the progressive establishment option between the two.

L1.e: Issues page: 'We should implement a modest wealth tax on the assets of billionaires and ultra-millionaires'

L3.e: Issues page: 'It's past time we had a national single-payer health system such as Medicare for All'; 'We need to pass Medicare for All'

L5.e: Issues page: 'We need to pass a Green New Deal'; will 'fight against federal authorization of new fossil fuel infrastructure'; No Fossil Fuel Money pledge

L6.e: Calls for 'Breaking up Amazon, Facebook, Google, and Apple' and for worker 'representation on corporate boards of large companies'

L7.e: Issues page: protect access to gender-affirming care, 'defend the right of individuals and families to make private medical decisions without the government interfering' and 'prevent states from passing discriminatory laws against transgender youth' (implies opposing state age limits; borderline)

L8.e: Would 'require platforms to strengthen safeguards against coordinated disinformation campaigns' and wants federal enforcement against 'misinformation tactics' (moderate-strength evidence)

L11.e: Calls for 'Abolishing the Electoral College' and moving to a national popular vote

C3.e: Backs a wealth tax, capital gains taxed as wages above $1M, higher corporate rate

EPD.note: State legislator 8 years and mayor of Evanston; MIT math PhD/ex-UChicago professor; very detailed issues platform naming bills (PRO Act, Stop Wall Street Looting Act, End Hedge Fund Control of American Homes Act, $17 minimum wage, 7% child-care cap) and an authored state record.

EO.note: Participated in numerous primary forums and the televised 25 Feb 2026 debate with Fine and Abughazaleh; no general-election debate with Republican John Elleson found. Gave interviews to NPR/WTTW and fielded hostile Jewish Insider coverage. Engaged substance on Israel (shifted on Iron Dome, defended conditioning aid: 'we cannot allow unconditional aid ... no matter what they do in Gaza').

outside_support: Opposed: AIPAC-aligned super PAC spending (millions against Biss, for Laura Fine)
notable_positions: Medicare for All / national single payer (https://www.danielbiss.com/issues/lowering-the-cost-of-essentials-putting-working-families-first)
'Modest wealth tax' on billionaires; tax capital gains as wages above $1M; raise corporate rate (https://www.danielbiss.com/issues/combating-income-inequality-by-taking-on-wealth-hoarding)
'We must abolish ICE' (https://www.danielbiss.com/issues/a-welcoming-immigration-policy)
Green New Deal; oppose new federal fossil-fuel infrastructure approvals (https://www.danielbiss.com/issues/protecting-our-democracy)
Break up Amazon/Facebook/Google/Apple; worker seats on corporate boards (https://www.danielbiss.com/issues/holding-big-tech-accountable)

Condition aid to Israel, back Block the Bombs Act, recognise a Palestinian state; supports Iron Dome funding (https://jewishinsider.com/2026/02/kat-abughazaleh-televised-debate-illinois-9th-congressional-district/)

He also has extensive credentials and debated actively, but the ideological markers are decisive.

Data-centre transparency and community-impact assessments before construction; opposed $650M data-centre tax incentives (https://www.electjdford.com/platform)

bio.prior_office: Andover Select Board 2019–2021; senior federal staff (Biden administration); lost 2018 MA-03 primary by ~145 votes

self_description: Fighter against Trump who takes 'the fight to MAGA directly' using 'facts ... not hyperbole'; leans on Biden-administration record.
primary_context: Won 6-way open primary (1 Sep 2026) with ~41% over state Rep. Tram Nguyen (29%, backed by Pressley, Trahan and Speaker Mariano), John Beccia, Jamie Belsito (Peace Action/Track AIPAC) and Beth Andres-Beck (Progressive Victory). Contest framed around Biden-era experience vs. affordability/economic justice rather than a sharp ideological split.

L9.e: Top-priority heading 'Abolish Trump's ICE' (body text calls for full overhaul of immigration system; qualifier 'Trump's' makes this weaker evidence)

C8.e: Will back legislation making it 'easier for people to secure permits needed to build additional housing' and zoning changes; backed by pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future/Think Big (~$700k TV)

EPD.note: Senior federal staff (Deputy Assistant to the President; Labor chief of staff) plus a local select-board term; Harvard MBA; numbered affordability plan ($10/day child care, 30%-of-income rent cap via renter's tax credit, 6% energy cap, worked family example), plus named bills (Freedom to Vote Act, Democracy for All Amendment).

EO.note: Primary-debate record not confirmed in sources reached (search budget exhausted). Seeks out hostile settings: says he has debated Scott Jennings on CNN and Tomi Lahren and appeared on Fox News Sunday. Argues with 'fact-based arguments ... not hyperbole'.

outside_support: Sens. Chris Coons and Andy Kim
Leading the Future / Think Big (pro-AI super PAC, ~$700k)
notable_positions: 'Medicare for All system that enrolls all Americans by default and preserves private insurance if desired' (not single payer replacing private insurance) (https://www.kohforcongress.com/issues/healthcare)
'Abolish Trump's ICE' / full immigration overhaul, more judges and asylum officers, expand legal pathways (https://www.kohforcongress.com/issues/your-issue-title-here)

Affordability plan: $10/day child care, rent capped at 30% of income via renter's credit, energy bills under 6% of income (https://www.kohforcongress.com/issues/delivering-affordability-for-the-north-shore)
Easier housing permits and zoning reform; expand LIHTC (https://www.kohforcongress.com/issues/affordable-housing)
No corporate PAC money; ban congressional stock trading; Democracy for All Amendment (https://www.kohforcongress.com/issues/issue-2)
Restore IRA climate credits and rejoin Paris (https://www.kohforcongress.com/issues/climate-change)
rationale: Biden-establishment candidate with progressive branding that he qualifies ('M4A' that preserves private insurance; 'Abolish Trump's ICE') plus pro-housing-supply and AI-industry backing, giving LI 1 and CI 1. Highly credentialed and unusually willing to engage hostile outlets (EPD 6, EO 4), so the rubric lands at step 5 'imperfect fit' with an LI/CI tie. Cat 4 is a weak nominal pick, and he could equally be read as mainstream-progressive.
